```{python}
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
prof = pd.read_csv("outputs/cluster_profiles.csv").set_index("cluster")
oy = pd.read_csv("outputs/outcomes_by_year.csv")
bins = pd.read_csv("outputs/irca_infant_bins.csv")
rho = pd.read_csv("outputs/irca_infant.csv").set_index("cluster")
import json
S = json.load(open("outputs/summary.json"))
names = prof["name"]
```

# Summary

Using `{python} f"{S['kept']:,}"` municipality-zone-year rows
(`{python} f"{S['municipalities']:,}"` municipalities, 2016-2023), k-means finds
`{python} S['k']` groups of municipal water profiles. The one with the highest
utility-supplied IRCA (median `{python} prof['irca_median'].max()`) is
"`{python} names[prof['irca_median'].idxmax()]`". Infant mortality, Saber 11 scores and
dropout differ across clusters, but these are **descriptive associations, not causal effects
of water quality**.

# Question

How do Colombian municipalities group by the safety of their drinking water and the
context around it, and how do infant mortality, school results and dropout look in each
group?

# Data

One row is a municipality x zone (urban/rural) x year, from the public dataset in
`data/` (INS, DNP TerriData, DANE, CHIRPS, ICFES, MEN; see Sources). **IRCA is the
utility-supplied ("prestadores") IRCA from INS open data**, not INS's national total; it
runs from 0 (no risk) to 100 (unfit) and is much more often missing for rural zones. Only
rows of municipalities with an IRCA value in 2016-2023 are used. Department capitals have
no urban/rural coverage split, so their urban coverage is filled from the municipal total
(`{python} S['capital_urban_rows_filled_from_total']` rows, flagged in the data).

# Method

Nine profile features (IRCA, water and sewer coverage, multidimensional poverty, rural
share, altitude, rainfall, municipal performance, log water transfers per person) were
standardised within each year and clustered with k-means
(`random_state` = `{python} S['seed']`, `{python} S['n_init']` starts). k = `{python} S['k']`
was chosen from the elbow, with silhouette `{python} round(S['silhouette_at_k'], 2)` and
stability across five seeds (ARI >= `{python} round(S['ari_min'], 3)`). Outcomes (infant
mortality, Saber 11, dropout) were **not** used to cluster; they only describe the clusters.

# What sets the clusters apart

```{python}
#| label: fig-heatmap
#| fig-cap: "Cluster mean z-scores (within year) of the nine profile features; blue is below the yearly average and red above."
#| fig-alt: "Heatmap with nine profile features as rows and four named clusters as columns, coloured from blue (below average) to red (above)."
zc = [c for c in prof.columns if c.startswith("z_")]
M = prof[zc].T; M.index = [c[2:] for c in zc]
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7.5, 4.4))
v = np.abs(M.values).max()
im = ax.imshow(M.values, cmap="RdBu_r", vmin=-v, vmax=v, aspect="auto")
ax.set_xticks(range(M.shape[1]))
ax.set_xticklabels([names[c].replace(", ", ",\n") for c in M.columns], fontsize=7)
ax.set_yticks(range(M.shape[0])); ax.set_yticklabels(M.index, fontsize=8)
for i in range(M.shape[0]):
    for j in range(M.shape[1]):
        ax.text(j, i, f"{M.values[i, j]:.1f}", ha="center", va="center", fontsize=7)
fig.colorbar(im, label="mean z-score"); plt.tight_layout(); plt.show()
```

# Outcomes by cluster

```{python}
#| label: fig-outcomes
#| fig-cap: "Median infant mortality (per 1,000 live births), Saber 11 mean score and school dropout (%) by cluster and year. Lines break where a source has no data."
#| fig-alt: "Three line charts, one per outcome, with one line per cluster from 2016 to 2023; lines have gaps in years without data."
outs = ["infant_mortality", "saber11_mean", "dropout_rate"]
years = np.arange(2016, 2024)
fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=(10, 3.4))
for ax, o in zip(axes, outs):
    for c, g in oy[oy["outcome"] == o].groupby("cluster"):
        s = g.set_index("year")["median"].reindex(years)
        ax.plot(years, s.values, marker="o", ms=3, color=prof.loc[c, "color"], label=names[c])
    ax.set_title(o, fontsize=9); ax.tick_params(labelsize=7)
fig.legend(*axes[0].get_legend_handles_labels(), loc="lower center", ncol=2, fontsize=6)
plt.tight_layout(rect=(0, 0.14, 1, 1)); plt.show()
```

Infant mortality changes method in 2017 and Saber 11 has no data for 2018 and 2021, so
year-to-year changes should not be read as real trends.

# Correlation is not causation

```{python}
#| label: fig-causation
#| fig-cap: "Median infant mortality (per 1,000 live births) by IRCA band (utility-supplied) within each cluster. Bars are medians; the Spearman rho between IRCA and infant mortality is in the legend."
#| fig-alt: "Grouped bar chart: for each IRCA band from no risk to unfit, four bars show median infant mortality in each cluster; the bars are similar in height within each cluster."
order = ["No risk", "Low", "Medium", "High", "Unfit"]
piv = bins.pivot(index="irca_band", columns="cluster", values="median").reindex(order)
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 3.8))
w = 0.2
for k, c in enumerate(piv.columns):
    ax.bar(np.arange(len(order)) + (k - 1.5) * w, piv[c].values, w, color=prof.loc[c, "color"],
           label=f"{names[c]} (rho = {rho.loc[c, 'spearman_rho']:.2f}, n = {rho.loc[c, 'n']})")
ax.set_xticks(range(len(order))); ax.set_xticklabels(order)
ax.set_xlabel("IRCA band (utility-supplied)"); ax.set_ylabel("median infant mortality")
ax.legend(fontsize=6); plt.tight_layout(); plt.show()
```

Within each cluster the association between IRCA and infant mortality is weak
(rho from `{python} f"{rho['spearman_rho'].min():.2f}"` to `{python} f"{rho['spearman_rho'].max():.2f}"`).
This is descriptive and does not establish a causal effect of water safety. Poverty, health
services, altitude and rurality may confound it.

# Limits

- Utility-supplied IRCA only; rural zones are often unsampled.
- Infant mortality changes method in 2017 and is volatile in small municipalities.
- Saber 11 covers 2014-2017, 2019, 2020 and 2022; school location is not residence.
- Missing coverage was imputed (year x zone median) in `{python} S['rows_with_any_imputed']` rows.
- Clusters are descriptive groupings, not causal categories.
